💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:07.
  • Mauricio Pochettino is keen to make significant behind-the-scenes changes at Manchester United following his arrival at Old Trafford.
  • The new Red Devils boss is understood to have identified a preferred candidate to replace sporting director Jason Wilcox, with whom he previously enjoyed a successful working relationship.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:07.

Mauricio Pochettino is keen to make significant behind-the-scenes changes at Manchester United following his arrival at Old Trafford.

The new Red Devils boss is understood to have identified a preferred candidate to replace sporting director Jason Wilcox, with whom he previously enjoyed a successful working relationship.

Paul Mitchell could now emerge as a leading contender for a return to football after previously being considered by INEOS.

According to reports, Pochettino has recommended Mitchell as United's next sporting director, believing the 45-year-old would be the ideal replacement for Wilcox.

The Argentine, who has signed a contract until June 2029, is said to have made his concerns about Wilcox clear during discussions with the club hierarchy before accepting the managerial position.

Wilcox has come under scrutiny following United's disappointing recent form and questions over the quality and depth of the squad assembled during his time at the club.

Pochettino is keen to work with someone he trusts, having previously enjoyed productive spells alongside Mitchell at Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur.

Mitchell was reportedly considered by INEOS for a senior football position in October 2023, before Wilcox ultimately took the role in April 2024.

Sources indicate that the 45-year-old recruitment chief also held positions at RB Leipzig and Monaco before spending 11 months as Newcastle's sporting director between 2024 and 2025. He has been out of football since departing St James' Park.

There are legitimate questions over whether Wilcox has delivered enough to justify remaining in such an influential position at Old Trafford.

United's summer recruitment has left several vital areas of the squad needing attention, particularly left-back and centre-forward, while the club have also struggled to generate funds by moving on unwanted players.

Marcus Rashford's situation is one example of the wider challenge of moving players who no longer fit the club's plans.

Furthermore, the decision to appoint Michael Carrick permanently before his eventual departure will inevitably come under scrutiny, especially given the responsibility placed on the sporting department to identify the right managerial appointment.

Mitchell would bring considerable recruitment experience and, crucially, an existing relationship with Pochettino.

INEOS should not make a change simply to satisfy a new manager, but if Wilcox has failed to provide the squad-building structure and recruitment strategy United need, replacing him could be a sensible step.

Pochettino needs a sporting director who shares his vision, and Mitchell could be a compelling candidate to help deliver that.

Sources indicate that “Now I don’t know if this staff has already been chosen, he keeps talking about new sporting directors, about new people who will join Milan. Let’s see what he can do. The promises are great, we’ll see what the results will be.”.

  • While Die Eisernen are languishing in the bottom three, Die Roten Bullen are eyeing up a fourth straight league victory as they continue to chase the Bundesliga’s top two.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sebastian Sternik | 20 Nov 2026 07:20.

Union Berlin are in the midst of their second-worst start to a Bundesliga season, and things are not about to get any easier as the relegation contenders prepare to host an in-form RB Leipzig side this Saturday afternoon.

While Die Eisernen are languishing in the bottom three, Die Roten Bullen are eyeing up a fourth straight league victory as they continue to chase the Bundesliga’s top two.

With just seven points to their name from their opening nine Bundesliga matches, Union Berlin are already feeling the pressure.

Head coach Mauro Lustrinelli survived the international break, with the club's hierarchy seemingly prepared to give the Swiss tactician more time to turn things around.

However, his long-term future remains far from certain, particularly after director Horst Heldt cast doubt over whether the 47-year-old would still be in charge over the next five months.

Heldt also revealed that Union are already drawing up looks for the January transfer window, although with more than a month to go before it opens, any potential reinforcements are unlikely to provide Lustrinelli with immediate relief.

What may help the Swiss coach is the fact Union’s best results this season have come at home, with 86% of all their points coming at the Stadion An der Alten Forsterei.

Nevertheless, Union's defensive problems overshadow any slight positives, given they have already conceded 21 goals - a new club record at this stage of a Bundesliga campaign.

While Union struggle to keep the ball out of the net, RB Leipzig simply cannot stop scoring at the moment.

Martin Demichelis and his men have already rattled the net 27 times in the Bundesliga this season - a total only bettered by Bayern Munich, who have scored on 29 occasions.

Just before the international break, Leipzig put five goals past Augsburg in a 5-2 victory - a game which extended their winning run to three straight league matches.

In recent times, Leipzig have also seen an upswing in their away results, winning their last two competitive games on the road - including a 2-0 success against Schalke at the end of October.

Striking early has been the key for Die Rotten Bullen so far this season, with the club yet to drop a point when scoring first in the Bundesliga.

In fact, the only major concern ahead of Saturday’s game is the fact Leipzig have lost four of their last six trips to Stadion An der Alten Forsterei.

Union Berlin form (all competitions):.

RB Leipzig form (all competitions):.

French defender Stanley Nsoki has missed every game this season for Union Berlin due to a muscle injury, and the 27-year-old will remain on the sidelines this weekend.

Robert Skov has only played one competitive minute this term, though he has recently returned to individual training.

Youngster Andrik Markgraf also remains out of action due to a knee injury, while Janik Haberer could miss Saturday’s game through illness.

When it comes to RB Leipzig, the visitors are also dealing with a handful of injuries as we head towards the end of the calendar year.

German midfielder Assan Ouedraogo has been out of action since September with a shoulder problem.

Youngsters Viggo Gebel and Marc Guiu are also dealing with knee and hamstring injuries.

Max Finkgrafe, meanwhile, has missed his last five games with a thigh injury, but is on the brink of a return.

Antonio Nusa, who has 11 goal contributions in nine Bundesliga games this season, is the man to watch for the visitors.

Union Berlin possible starting lineup:.

Ronnow; Juranovic, Van den Bosch, Friedrich, Rothe; Imeri, Schafer, Khedira, Aebischer; Ilic, Burke.

RB Leipzig possible starting lineup:.

Vandevoordt; Baku, Orban, Lukeba, Raum; El Aynaoui, Banzuzi; Gruda, Nkunku, Nusa; Romulo.

Union Berlin perform a lot better at home, but that may not be enough to stop a rampant RB Leipzig side that simply cannot stop scoring goals.

The visitors smell blood as they continue to chase the top two, and there is a strong possibility that things could get ugly in Berlin.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:14 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 10:33 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Manchester United have released their latest financial results after spending another £15million to install Mauricio Pochettino as the club’s latest head coach.
  • United’s first quarter financials up to September 30 don’t include the cost of paying the US Soccer Federation £10m to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts, or an additional £5m to pay off Michael Carrick and his staff.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 08:14 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 10:33 EST, 19 November 2026.

Manchester United have released their latest financial results after spending another £15million to install Mauricio Pochettino as the club’s latest head coach.

United’s first quarter financials up to September 30 don’t include the cost of paying the US Soccer Federation £10m to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts, or an additional £5m to pay off Michael Carrick and his staff.

They show that United brought in total revenues of £146.1m compared to £140.3m in the first quarter last year, but made an operating loss for the quarter of £3m compared with an operating profit of £13m 12 months ago.

The results come just weeks after co-owner Avram Glazer told a conference that the club’s value is not dependent on success on the pitch.

Sources say that United acted early in the season to address the drop in form under Carrick that saw United slide into the relegation zone, and the club are now focused on improving results under Pochettino.

The Argentine is expected to be given a modest transfer budget in January to make upcoming signings, with United in the market for a striker, left-back and centre-back.

Man United's latest financial results come after the Glazers stated that success isn't dependent on results.

The results don't include the £10m United paid to buy Pochettino and his staff from the US national team.

Chief executive Omar Berrada said: ‘Our revenue remains strong and on track, while we continue to grow sustainably. We are pleased to welcome Mauricio Pochettino and his staff to the club and our priority is to support them as we look continuously to improve our performances on the pitch.’.

Sources indicate that the latest results only cover the first five Premier League fixtures of the season, one Champions League match and the League Cup defeat to Brighton. Sources insist that they show the benefit of the cost-cutting under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos and what they say is improved operational efficiency.

United have reiterated their guidance of total revenues of £740-£760m for this financial year after reporting that the first quarter saw rises in broadcast (£5.3m), retail (£1.3m) and matchday (£0.6m) revenues.

However, sponsorship revenue was down by £1.4m despite a new training kit deal with Betway, largely due to United playing individual pre-season friendlies rather than going on summer tour.

Employee benefit expenses for the quarter were £79.9m, an increase of £6.3m due mainly to players' wages going up 25 per cent after qualifying for the Champions League.

United's borrowing has increased 19 per cent from a year ago, with the club's historic US dollar debt up $125m to $775m 'as a result of the refinancing of our senior secured notes in June 2026'.

This rise, which was revealed in the last set of results in September, equates to £577.4m, up from £481.2m. The net cost of financing that debt dropped from £21.4m to £14.5m.

Meanwhile, United’s borrowing on the club's revolving credit facility was £207.1m as of September 30, down from £268m a year ago.

Chelsea have seen their hopes of signing Juventus youngster Kerim Alajbegovic hit a major stumbling block ahead of the January transfer window.

The Blues were previously interested in the teenager during the summer, with Blues boss Xabi Alonso having monitored his development closely during his time in charge of Bayer Leverkusen.

However, Juventus are determined to keep hold of the highly-rated winger, with a potential departure currently considered off the table.

Alajbegovic was pursued by Chelsea during the summer after impressing at RB Salzburg, but the west London club's proposed project failed to convince the youngster.

The Blues were understood to be considering sending him out on loan rather than offering immediate first-team opportunities, allowing the Serie A giants to secure his signature instead.

There has now been renewed interest from Alonso's side, but reports in Italy (via Sport Witness) suggest Chelsea face an uphill battle to bring the 19-year-old maestro to Stamford Bridge.

It is claimed that Alajbegovic 'isn't leaving' Juventus, with the Italian side pleased by his development and unwilling to consider an exit despite interest from England.

The £30m teenager is also happy with his role in Turin, where he believes he has the right environment to continue developing, with similar reports suggesting that he wants to remain at Juventus for a 'long time'.

As a result, an immediate departure has been described as 'truly barred', making a January transfer particularly difficult to negotiate.

Chelsea's interest is understandable given the Bosnian's potential, but the club may struggle to convince him that Stamford Bridge is the right place for his development.

Regular first-team football should be a priority for a teenager at this stage of his career, and Juventus are currently providing him with opportunities to establish himself.

By contrast, Chelsea's sizeable squad creates greater competition for attacking positions, with even highly-rated youngster Estevao having experienced his own difficulties securing consistent game time.

That situation could serve as a warning to Alajbegovic, particularly when he is already enjoying an increasingly prominent role in Turin.

Although Juventus may not offer the most stable environment, they are giving the youngster opportunities to develop at senior level.

Chelsea might be able to offer a lucrative project, but unless they can guarantee a clearer pathway into the first team, Alajbegovic would arguably be better off remaining in Italy.

By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:51.

Tottenham Hotspur are considering a 'surprise' move for Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap as Roberto De Zerbi looks to strengthen his attacking options.

The 23-year-old has revived his career at the City Ground following a difficult spell at Chelsea, attracting renewed interest from north London.

However, a potential deal could be more complicated than initially expected, with Forest placing a substantial valuation on their summer signing.

According to FootballTransfers, Delap is 'admired' by De Zerbi, with Spurs continuing to monitor the former Ipswich Town forward after tracking him during the summer transfer window.

Delap has scored three goals in his first nine Premier League appearances for Forest, offering encouraging signs following his disappointing spell at Stamford Bridge.

A January move is considered extremely difficult, though, given Forest only signed him in the summer and are unlikely to sanction his departure while fighting for their Premier League status.

Tricky Trees owner Evangelos Marinakis is not expected to approve a mid-season sale, although it is understood that De Zerbi could be prepared to wait until the summer of 2027.

Forest are likely to demand around £75m for the Englishman, which would represent a significant profit on the initial £45m they paid Chelsea.

There is no denying that Delap has shown some improvement at Forest, but his overall Premier League goalscoring record remains a significant concern amid Spurs' renewed interest.

His three goals this season take his career total to just 16 efforts in 76 Premier League outings, while he managed only three goals in 47 appearances for Chelsea.

Those numbers hardly suggest a striker capable of immediately resolving Tottenham's attacking problems, particularly if Forest demand £75m to part with him.

Spurs still need a reliable source of goals if they are to climb the table and compete for major honours, rather than another expensive gamble on potential.

De Zerbi's admiration is understandable, but Tottenham should be wary of paying a premium for a forward whose top-flight returns remain underwhelming.

Delap may yet develop into an excellent striker, but spending that much on him would represent a considerable risk for a club with more pressing needs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southampton have fought their way back up the Championship table and into play-off contention despite a four-point deduction at the start of the season, as head coach Tonda Eckert may already have one eye on the upcoming January transfer window.

In what is now old news, Southampton were deducted four points at the start of the Championship campaign after being found guilty of spying on opponents last season, and were also thrown out of the play-offs as a result.

This time around, the Saints are looking to claw their way into the top eight legitimately with Eckert still at the helm, and following eight wins, four draws, and three defeats after 15 league games, they are well within play-off contention.

The German boss has stamped his authority at St Mary's following the summer transfer window, though not every addition has necessarily worked out the way he would've hoped.

Southampton saw the likes of Shea Charles, Taylor Harwood-Bellis, Cameron Archer, and Ben Brereton Diaz head out of the St Mary's exit door over the summer, as the likes of Lewis Dobbin, James Ward-Prowse, Keven Schlotterbeck, and Divin Mubama joined in the opposite direction.

Mubama, 21, joined on loan from Manchester City after spending the previous campaign on loan with Stoke City in the Championship, with the England youth international expecting to push Canadian striker Cyle Larin hard for a place in the starting XI.

Divin Mubama Stoke City Championship statistics 2025/26 (Data as per FotMob).

However, despite his 13 league appearances thus far, only one of those has come as a start, with Mubama being limited to just over 200 minutes of league football so far this campaign, struggling to make an impact in those limited minutes.

Naturally, his parent club, Man City, won't be pleased by his lack of game time and subsequent development, as Football League World has taken a look at two Championship clubs that should consider rescuing the 21-year-old this winter.

Derby County find themselves in the midst of a scrap towards the foot of the Championship table as things stand, with two wins, four draws, and nine defeats in their opening 15 league games piling pressure on head coach John Eustace.

A 3-1 home victory over Bolton Wanderers just before the international break has seemingly given Eustace a lifeline at Pride Park, and if his side can start to pick up some form, he may well start turning his attention to the January transfer window sooner rather than later.

Up top, Derby can boast the likes of Carlton Morris, Henrik Meister, and Lars-Jorgen Salvesen, whilst both Patrick Agyemang, Mohammed Fuseini, and Rhian Brewster can also operate in that position; on the face of it, a fresh centre-forward option is not needed.

However, those six options have just five goals between them at this stage in the season, and whilst numerous factors can be attributed to this, Derby simply cannot afford to settle with what they have got.

The Rams, according to Pete O'Rourke via X, were closing in on a move for Mubama earlier on in the summer window, but for one reason or another, the deal never went through, and the England youth international headed to Southampton instead.

The sort of centre-forward that Eustace loves: quick, strong, capable of holding up the ball and interlinking play as well as getting in behind, and with smart movement, Mubama would be an excellent addition for Derby, and if he can be provided with chances regularly, he will help the Rams look towards the play-offs instead of the relegation zone.

Would you like to see Divin Mubama at your club? Do you agree with our picks? Where do you think he should go? Share your thoughts below!

Mubama spent the bulk of his youth playing days in the West Ham United academy, going on to make 18 first-team appearances for the Hammers and scoring once before heading to Man City in the summer of 2024 for just £1.2 million compensation.

West Ham have endured a tricky start to life back in the Championship, with Nuno Espírito Santo being handed his marching orders after 13 games and being replaced by former Fulham, Bournemouth, and Burnley boss Scott Parker.

Parker made over a century of appearances for the East London outfit during his playing days, and it is hoped that he can steer the club in the right direction following his appointment.

The former England midfielder may well already have one eye on the January transfer window, with Alan Nixon having recently reported via Patreon that West Ham are targeting a new striker and left-back this winter.

Taty Castellanos and Pablo Felipe have not handled the drop into the second tier especially well, as Joel Piroe has emerged as the preferred option up front as things stand, though the Dutchman could do with some competition.

As a cheap loan, and a player who understands exactly what the West Ham DNA is, Mubama would be a solid fit for the Hammers and would offer a completely different profile to Piroe.

If Castellanos and Pablo leave, a latest striker will be needed regardless, and following his lack of minutes with Southampton, Parker has the opportunity to show the Saints exactly what they've been missing out on with a January swoop.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roberto Di Matteo has admitted that he was ‘shocked’ West Brom sacked him back in 2011 as they battled to stay in the Premier League.

The Italian had a successful playing career, and he turned to management after retiring, initially starting out with MK Dons.

A move to Albion would follow, and Di Matteo would also work for Chelsea, Schalke and Aston Villa, with the high point undoubtedly coming with the Blues, who he won the Champions League and FA Cup with as interim boss.

Whilst nothing will surpass winning those trophies with Chelsea, Di Matteo really made his name as a manager during his time at The Hawthorns with West Brom.

After making the step up from League One outfit MK Dons, Di Matteo built an Albion side that won promotion to the Premier League in his first season at the club.

Recent findings suggest that they did so by playing a brand of football that the fans really enjoyed, and they carried that into the top flight. Whilst an opening day 6-0 defeat at Chelsea was concerning, the players swiftly adapted to the Premier League.

The Baggies had picked up 15 points from their first nine games, which included a memorable 3-2 win at Arsenal, a 2-2 draw at Old Trafford, and they also picked up a point from Tottenham.

So, Albion were performing very well, and they continued the entertaining style of play that had made them such a good watch the season before.

However, that form didn’t continue, and Di Matteo was ultimately dismissed in February, after a miserable period of seven defeats in nine.

And, speaking to Mick McCarthy and Tony Pulis on The Managers podcast, Di Matteo couldn’t hide how disappointed he was at the decision, with Albion outside the relegation zone at the time.

According to recent reports, “I was a bit surprised and shocked. We’ve all worked in smaller clubs, so when you have injuries to one or two key players, it’s difficult. Up until the Christmas period we were looking really good, but Jonas Olsson, the centre-back, got injured for a while, and one or two others were not available.

Sources indicate that “In the Christmas period, you play every two or three days and you don’t have a deep squad, so you struggle a bit. But, again, we were coming out of it, and I was really shocked.”.

You can understand why Di Matteo was surprised at the decision, as he will have been tasked with keeping the team in the league, and he will argue he was on track to do that.

Plus, this was the first tough spell he had in charge of Albion, so he would’ve hoped that he had enough credit in the bank to be given an opportunity to turn things around.

Yet, football is a ruthless business, and the Albion board needed to make what they felt was the best decision for the club, and the reality is that, in hindsight, it was a call that paid off.

They had been on a terrible run over a period of a few months, and they would say the trend was pointing towards relegation.

In a recent development, west Brom fans, how do you reflect on Roberto Di Matteo's time in charge? Let us know in the comments below.

As it turns out, West Brom appointed Roy Hodgson, in what was a masterstroke. He kept the team up with ease, and they had another seven consecutive years as a Premier League before relegation in 2018.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sebastian Sternik | 20 Nov 2026 08:09.

Saturday night entertainment in the Bundesliga will come from the Veltins Arena in Gelsenkirchen, as Schalke 04 welcome Stuttgart for a tasty league encounter.

The hosts have endured a dreadful start to the season and are still looking to score their first home goal, while the visitors are setting their sights on a third successive league success.

Schalke ended their five-match goalless run last time out against Hoffenheim, although their attacking breakthrough counted for little as they suffered a 2-1 defeat.

That result left Die Konigsblauen sitting in the relegation zone during the international break, while head coach Miron Muslic avoided an early sack.

Nevertheless, the 44-year-old remains under considerable pressure, with Schalke now enduring a seven-game winless streak across all competitions.

Even more concerning for the Royal Blues faithful is the fact that their points tally after nine Bundesliga matches is identical to the one they recorded at the same stage of their disastrous 2022-23 campaign, which ended in relegation.

In order to turn things around, the hosts will need to start scoring goals, otherwise they risk becoming just the second team in Bundesliga history to go without a goal across their first five home matches of a season.

There is one positive for the hosts and that is the fact they beat Stuttgart when these two teams last met back in February 2023 - their only victory over the Swabians in five previous meetings.

While Schalke are on the ropes, Stuttgart are on the attack, with the Swabians looking to record their third straight Bundesliga win.

Sebastian Hoeness and his side powered to a 1-0 win over Werder Bremen just before the international break, leaving them just six points adrift of the top four.

Given their sluggish start to the campaign, Stuttgart's recent upturn represents a welcome change in fortunes, with their defensive improvements playing a significant role.

Two clean sheets from their last three domestic outings make for much better reading than the two shutouts they managed across their opening 10 matches of the season.

Stuttgart will now turn their attention to landing their first league win over Schalke since 2021 - the only success over the Royal Blues they boast in 12 previous meetings.

What’s more, the Swabians have not managed to win at the Veltins Arena since 2013 - losing four and drawing three of their last seven trips to Gelsenkirchen.

Stuttgart form (all competitions):.

Along with their goalscoring problems, Schalke are also dealing with a lengthy injury list.

Maximilian Wober and youngster Luca Vozar are both right now out with hamstring injuries.

Defender Timo Becker picked up a foot problem just before the international break, and will also remain on the sidelines.

Emil Hojlund is yet to feature for Schalke this season due to an Achilles injury, while midfielder Ron Schallenberg is out with a leg problem.

Stuttgart are also missing a handful of names, including midfielder Angelo Stiller who is struggling with an adductor injury.

Swiss defender Luca Jaquez featured in the 1-0 win over Bremen before the international break, but he has since become a doubt due to a ribs problem.

Youngsters Jarzinho Malanga and Justin Diehl complete the injury list, with the two players carrying thigh and abdominal issues.

Meanwhile, forward Deniz Undav missed out on selection for the German national team, with the 30-year-old still looking for his first Bundesliga goal this season.

Stuttgart possible starting lineup:.

Seimen; Hendriks, Chabot, Mittelstadt; Leweling, Karazor, Promel, Fuhrich; El Khannouss, Undav; Demirovic.

Schalke are simply not scoring at home, and they could struggle here against an improving Stuttgart defence.

The visitors have struggled away in Gelsenkirchen over the years, but this is the perfect opportunity to improve that record.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City's 2026/27 season has got off to a remarkable start on the pitch, with supporters starting to dream about what might be possible under Chris Davies.

The 41-year-old previously split opinion amongst Blues fans, especially after the way in which the 2025/26 Championship season panned out following continued investment from Knighthead Capital Management.

The club's American investors have vowed to change plenty in such a short space of time, and that doesn't just concern the outlook of Davies' squad in the near future as they chase a Premier League return, but the city of Birmingham as a whole.

Tom Wagner has been heralded for the work he has already put in and what he is planning towards as Blues look to finally realise their potential.

The idea of looking at the past to move forward can often be frowned upon, but for Wagner and Co. doing exactly that means that Birmingham fans are never likely to lose sight of their identity as the club embarks on a new era.

Last season may have been one of mixed fortunes for Birmingham and their supporters on the pitch, but that didn't mean it wasn't historic in other ways.

Sources indicate that indeed, just days before Blues celebrated their 150th anniversary game with a 4-1 rout over Norwich City, the club unveiled the design and name of its upcoming 62,500-seater stadium, which will stand tall less than a mile away from St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park.

The Powerhouse will pay tribute to the Second City's rich industrial heritage, embodied by its name and design, and that comes across in more ways than one.

The Powerhouse will be the centrepiece of a multi-billion Sports Quarter project that will transform the Bordesley Green area with multiple commercial and retail hubs adjacent to the stadium.

Whilst the chimney-themed design has received major criticism from rival fanbases and beyond, those associated with the club will love how it will repurpose some of Birmingham's rich history.

Over 1,000 bricks which helped structure the City Hospital in Winson Green - built in 1912 as Birmingham Workhouse Infirmary - are being repurposed for the Powerhouse to stand tall on the former site of the Adderley Park Brickworks.

Recent findings suggest that blues fans, how excited are you to move into the Powerhouse? Comment below!

Sources indicate that city Hospital has been closed since 2024, with the former site making way for a 750-home development adjacent to the Birmingham and Wolverhampton Main Line Canal, approximately 4.1 miles away from St. Andrew's.

"Lovingly salvaged, cleaned, sorted and restored by local experts, the original bricks from Adderley Park Brickworks will be incorporated into the Powerhouse – Birmingham City's future home and a defining part of the city’s Sports Quarter," a section of a statement on Blues' website confirming the purchase of noted bricks read.

In recent months, more work has gone into how the overall Sports Quarter and the Powerhouse stadium will look ahead of a planned opening in the summer of 2031.

Many Blues fans are excited by what is to come, as emotional as it will be when the club have to leave St. Andrew's, having called their current stadium home since the year 1906.

In May, mutiple 'CGI' images were generated and shared by Birmingham's official social media accounts, including how various hospitality packages will be incorporated into the chimney designs.

This includes a high-level view of the pitch which will be named the 'Chimney Seats', as well as 'Restaurant with a View', which will allow guests a view of the city's main skyline, which stands approximately two miles away.

As previously mentioned, Knighthead have certainly done their utmost to embrace themselves in various cultural aspects associated with the West Midlands.

The Sports Quarter will provide thousands of jobs for locals, whilst also increasing the economy. In the meantime, the investment firm has also acquired stakes in Birmingham Phoenix alongside former Blues academy graduate and Real Madrid star, Jude Bellingham.

In a recent development, the effort which has gone into such a transformative project has not been underestimated by Blues fans, and it has been particularly evident how they feel about Wagner in his recent returns to St. Andrew's after unfortunately suffering a stroke in January.

Charlie Austin believes Blackburn Rovers will be determined to beat Burnley for Tony Mowbray when the two rivals meet on Sunday.

It has been a tough few days for Rovers, as the club announced that Mowbray had stepped back from his role as head coach due to health complications.

Many had tipped Blackburn for relegation before a ball was kicked this season, but they have enjoyed a very positive campaign so far under Mowbray, with the team going into the weekend fixtures just three points outside the play-off places.

Therefore, news of Mowbray’s health issues is a real setback for the club, although it obviously puts football into perspective, with the football world coming together to wish the ex-Middlesbrough chief well.

And, speaking on his Chaz Kicks Off podcast, former Burnley striker Austin echoed those thoughts, and he also explained why the news will unite the Rovers group going into the game.

In a recent development, “When anybody gets ill, or has issues in their personal life, you wish them all the best. But you see from all the players and people that know him, that have made comments, it reveals what kind of bloke he is.

“Blackburn’s teamtalk is done. It’s an easy one to say, let’s win this for the manager, let’s win it for Mowbray. He’s got more important things going on in his life, which puts football second, but let's go and give everything. Not 110%, but as a collective, let's give 150% and go and run over our neighbours Burnley and make a big statement.

“That’s how I’d see it if I was in the Blackburn dressing room, and it’d be the same if I was a coach or a fan - go and put on a performance for Mowbray.”.

This news came as a shock to the Rovers supporters, so it presumably was the same for the players, and, as Austin says, the initial reaction is to send your thoughts to Mowbray.

But, football will go on, and it’s inevitable that the Blackburn group will want to get results for the manager, as he was a hugely respected figure at the club, and he has personally helped so many of the current squad.

It’s not like they need extra motivation to beat Burnley when you consider the hatred that comes with the East Lancashire derby anyway, but, if they did, then this will provide it, and you can be sure that Mowbray’s name will be spoken about before the players go out on Sunday.

Of course, the coaching staff won’t want to add too much emotional pressure to the players, so they must channel it properly, but the Blackburn squad will head to Turf Moor with full belief that they can pick up three points.

This is a fixture that the Clarets have dominated recently, with Burnley having not lost to their rivals in the last 11 attempts, which is a run that stretches back to 2010.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. In a recent development, “I love those challenges,” mentioned Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, peterborough United appointed Robbie Savage as their fresh manager on October 2nd, having been impressed by the work he'd done with Forest Green Rovers. His ex-Leicester City teammate, Emile Heskey, has now offered a peak behind the curtain to reveal exactly what the Posh boss is like.

Savage is still juggling his life as a pundit and media personality, alongside the full-time gig with Peterborough in League One.

Naturally, there's been some opposition to that arrangement, and a run of seven games in all competitions without a win heading into this weekend isn't exactly helping his cause.

Ironically, Savage's first game as Peterborough boss came against Leicester on October 10th, with his side racing into a 3-0 lead before seeing the game out to win 3-1, giving the former Fox the ideal start to life in the dugout.

After coming through at Man United and cutting his teeth with Crewe, it had been at Leicester where Savage had made a name for himself in the Premier League.

Heskey has been appearing on the 'Jamie Vardy's Having A Party' podcast, with the two former Leicester strikers trading stories from their time at the club.

In one part, Heskey is quizzed on any 'funny stories' he might have from his time at Filbert Street, where he responds to talk about Savage turning up in a purple Porsche, which Vardy finds easy to believe.

Sources indicate that vardy says: "Stuff like that brings the team together. He’s set himself up, but it’s good for the group.".

Heskey totally agrees, saying: "He was really good in taking it (the banter he got)," before revealing to a surprised Vardy: "He actually is quite sensitive and very insecure is Robbie.

Industry observers note that "He’s one of those players where, before a game, we’d have to say, ‘We need you, Robbie, come on. You’re the best’.

Recent findings suggest that "He’d be nervous and like he didn’t want to play, pulling out of games. But this is this happy-go-lucky guy that you see all bubbly and that, but he is quite insecure.".

Heskey played with Savage at Leicester, before also linking up with him at Birmingham City later in the pair's careers.

As Heskey reveals, Savage was good at taking things on the chin when it came to the banter he got in the changing rooms. He was also pretty good at doing the same thing from rival fans as a player.

Sources indicate that savage finished his Leicester career with 204 appearances for the Foxes, along with 137 at Derby County, 100 at Blackburn Rovers and a further 88 for Birmingham. 346 of his career outings came in the Premier League, and you can tell by the tone of Heskey's voice that he picked up a fair bit of admiration for that.

Moving into coaching isn't easy, but Savage has had stints with Macclesfield and Forest Green, cutting his teeth at the bottom of the game to earn this chance at Peterborough.

It's a slightly different persona he will have to give off as a manager compared to a player, but every inch of his experience will be key to turning things around for Posh.

Barry Bannan has issued a two-word reaction to the performance of Sheffield Wednesday teammate, Jamal Lowe, as the Owls made it two league victories in succession under newly-appointed head coach, Dave Challinor.

Having seen off Plymouth Argyle last Saturday, Challinor's first League One outing in charge of Wednesday on the road came in the form of a South Yorkshire derby against Daniel Stendel's lowly Barnsley outfit.

Backed by over 4,800 supporters, Challinor's side didn't disappoint as they raced into a two-goal lead within the first 14 minutes, with Lowe netting his first brace of the campaign.

The Tykes responded five minutes before half-time through the highly-rated Vimal Yonganathan, but back-to-back victories for the first time since September lifted the Owls up to third.

Upon taking the managerial role at Hillsborough, Challinor has plenty of quality and experience at his disposal, with both attributes possessed by Bannan and Lowe in particular.

The latter opened the scoring at Oakwell just eight minutes into the encounter as he side-footed Liam Cooper's knockdown from a free-kick past Cieran Slicker, before doubling the advantage six minutes later as he was found in acres of space by Bannan, then drifting inside and slotting the ball into the bottom-right-hand corner.

Those strikes were the Jamaican's first since his dramatic 98th-minute penalty against Huddersfield Town last month, taking his overall tally up to seven for the season.

Speaking post-match, Lowe claimed that he is capable of taking his tally up to 15 goals, which will be music to the ears of Owls fans, as well as Bannan, who issued a two-word reaction of: "Goals Like", with a picture of him and the versatile figure in celebration.

Across his 93 appearances for the Owls, Lowe has endured a mixed time, even after producing seven goal contributions last term.

In the wins over Plymouth and Barnsley, the 32-year-old has been stationed at left-wing-back, and received praise for his all-round performance from many Wednesdayites.

"Testament to the newly introduced manager people say oh J Lowe is lazy can’t run etc and not only does Dave have him run he puts him at LWB where he has to run and gets goals from there on top," said one of those supporters.

It has been revealed that another Wednesday fan commented: "Gave Jamal Lowe stick last couple of weeks but effort for tonight was brilliant. Credit where credits due well done 2 goals along the way! Long may it continue. Honolulu Wednesday!!!".

"Jamal Lowe has turned into peak Roberto Carlos," was a rather humourous summation of his exploits.

Owls fans, how did you view Jamal Lowe's all-round performance against Barnsley? Comment below!

Sources indicate that another verdict read: "Playing Lowe in (his) best position. GOAL. Well done Jamz.".

However, not all were overly convinced, with one supporter claiming: "Lowe has no clue how to defend.".

Challinor recently went viral due to an image of his notes during the FA Cup defeat to Oldham Athletic in his first game in charge, and despite a youthful side being defeated heavily in the EFL Trophy to Accrington Stanley, his league ventures have started strongly.

Wednesday are still not flawless, but the outlook of their season is certainly more rosey than in the final weeks of Henrik Pedersen's tenure, as they can only drop to fifth depending on Saturday's results.

With Plymouth expected to challenge for promotion, last weekend's 3-0 success was seen as a statement, whilst different characteristics earned three points against their local rivals.

Challinor will now hope his side benefit from an extra day's recovery for when they travel to Stevenage on Tuesday.

The new Sheffield Wednesday manager had qualified praise for his team's performance following his team's South Yorkshire derby win at Barnsley.

In a recent development, following a slightly rocky start, Dave Challinor is starting to settle in as the new manager of Sheffield Wednesday. Two Jamal Lowe goals in the opening stages of their Friday night trip to Barnsley gave them the perfect start at Oakwell, but Wednesday were pegged back by a goal from Vimal Yoganathan and ended up hanging on a little for the win.

The three points lifted them to third place in the table, though as this was a Friday night fixture, they might well not still be there by the end of the weekend, and after the match Challinor had some praise for his team's performance, though he was very clear that they still have a lot of work to do to get the team to the level of the manager's satisfaction.

Speaking to the Sheffield Wednesday media team after his team's win at Barnsley as posted to the social media platfiorm X, Challinor was qualified in praise of his team's performance: "I'm really pleased with the win. I won't say I'm disappointed with our performance, but I think there's loads more to come from us. As I've just said to the players, my job's not to really over-celebrate wins, it's to look at things analytically and make sure we're better, and there's stacks more to come from us.".

Sources indicate that and it's clear that Challinor wants to see his team playing on the front foot more: "Scoring two goals is the best thing that could happen and probably the worst thing too because, from a player's perspective, we became really passive, too negative, and almost thought the game was won. We have and will continue to take ourselves out of our comfort zone and expose ourselves a little bit. We need to defend miles higher up.".

It has been revealed that what tweaks would you want made to the Sheffield Wednesday team during the January transfer window? Let us know in the comments below!

Recent findings suggest that asked about the performance of Jamal Lowe, Challinor revealed that the forward was disappointed not to receive the Man of the Match Award, given his two goals: "It's nice to score from a set-piece again. Jamal's done another brilliant job for the team in a position that's not his position, but he's got two goals from there, which is great for him, and on another day he gets himself a hat-trick, potentially. Strangely, he hasn't got the Match of the Match from Sky, which he's disappointed about, but we can deal with that because we've got three points.".

And he also singled out Liam Cooper for praise: "Coops is a leader for us. With him, his experience and his age, he is going to be notable, but as I've told him, I've got to get him to get the rest of them up the pitch and not be defending too deep. I've been there. The last thing you want to be is a centre-half who's not rapid against strikers who want to run in behind, looking behind and having loads of space between your backside and your own goal. But it's going to paramount to what we do and how we go about it. And for him to get through two 90 minutes in the last week is brilliant for us. We've got to recover and make sure we're good to go on Tuesday.".

Dave Challinor's post-Barnsley comments have provoked a positive reaction from Sheffield Wednesday fans who are pleased to hear him not settling after a win:.

And this Wednesday fan echoes that sentiment:.

This fans feels that the first-team squad does need strengthening in the latest year:.

And this Wednesday fan believes that Challinor is a clear upgrade on his predecessor:.

Sheffield Wednesday's 2-1 win at Barnsley continued their uplift under Dave Challinor. Defeat away to League Two Oldham Athletic in the FA Cup was not the result that anyone at Hillsborough was expecting from his first match in charge, but his team has recovered well in the two games since then, with a convincing 3-0 win against Plymouth Argyle in his first home match as manager followed by a welcome derby win away from home at Barnsley.

Sources indicate that the win pushed Wednesday up to third place in the League One table, though it's unlikely they'll still be there by the end of the weekend. Fourth-placed Oxford United are at home to Wycombe Wanderers, while fifth-placed Luton Town are away to Burton Albion. Wins for both of them would drop Sheffield Wednesday back to fifth place in the League One table again.

But Dave Challinor is an experienced enough manager to know that league positions don't matter too much at this point of the season. What matters more is the direction of travel that the team are in under their newly introduced manager, and two straight wins strongly suggests that Sheffield Wednesday are heading in the right direction under him.

And the reaction of the Sheffield Wednesday fans makes clear that the manager's desire to uphold the highest standards is exactly what they need at the moment too. Wednesday fans had an awful time of things in the Championship last season, and when backs are against the wall in that way, upholding standards on the pitch could come to feel like the last thing on anybody's mind. As such this sort of reaction to a win from the manager might be considered a reflection upon normality returning to Hillsborough, as the team continues to push for a quick return to the second tier.

The 54-year-old replaces Michael Carrick, who was dismissed last week after United won just one of their opening 10 Premier League matches, leaving them 18th in the table.

Pochettino arrives after completing his final assignment with the United States, who beat Haiti 2-0 on Tuesday to secure an 8-0 aggregate victory in their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final.

The Argentine has signed a contract until the summer of 2029 and is expected to meet his latest players and oversee his first training session on Thursday.

Speaking after his final match with the United States, Pochettino acknowledged the challenge awaiting him in Manchester.

“The newly introduced challenge is a significant challenge, but at the same time it’s adrenaline you want to feel,” he said.

In a recent development, several members of his coaching staff, including long-time assistant Jesus Perez, travelled to Manchester earlier this week to begin preparations. Pochettino will have limited time to work with his squad before Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Liverpool, which kicks off at 4.30pm GMT.

The former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain manager inherits a United side struggling for results after a difficult opening to the campaign. He previously guided Tottenham to the 2019 Champions League final and won the French league title during his spell with Paris Saint-Germain.

United’s next fixtures also include a Champions League trip to Sporting CP and a home Premier League match against Brentford. Pochettino’s immediate task is to improve United’s league position, beginning with a demanding first match at Anfield.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 08:16 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

Premier League clubs have voted to protect the organisation's bigwigs from any individual legal action taken by Manchester City's sponsors.

Instead, the clubs - including City themselves - will foot any legal bills incurred by a potential corporate defamation suit.

Daily Mail Sport understands there was widespread support from clubs to insulate Premier League chief executive Richard Masters and the four other league directors.

The vote passed with 18 clubs in favour, and City and Nottingham Forest against.

It is understood Forest opted to vote that way as they felt they had not been given sufficient information or enough time to consider the proposal and its implications, as opposed to representing a show of support for City.

The matter was the first item on the agenda at the Premier League shareholders' meeting in the Savoy Hotel on Thursday and was addressed promptly with limited discussion.

Clubs had a paper for the proposed rule change before the meeting and there was significant support to extend the legal protection to individuals on the league's board.

This marks the first time since the Premier League’s inception that insurance arrangements for its board members have been reviewed.

Premier League clubs will foot the bill if Manchester City's sponsors sue for defamation.

In September, City were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules after a seven-year legal process.

An independent commission appointed by the Premier League found City inflated their revenues by £900million – disguising money from their Abu Dhabi ownership group as sponsorship revenue.

Etihad Airways, owned by the Abu Dhabi government, denied being ‘involved in improper commercial arrangements’ and noted it was considering legal action in response to the verdict.

Meanwhile, another City sponsor, Etisalat - a telecommunications company - is also weighing up legal action.

City, though, maintain their innocence and are appealing the decision, which could see them relegated from the top flight.

After leaving Manchester United in 2022, the midfielder continued his career with Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and Western Sydney Wanderers before joining Melbourne Victory in September 2025.

Recent findings suggest that his final season in Australia was an impressive one. Mata registered five goals and 13 assists, won the Johnny Warren Medal and earned a place in the A-League Team of the Season.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the major shifts to domestic football in the last thirty years comes in the form of football hooliganism, which has received particular police attention and continues to be clamped down by the authorities.

The hooliganism subculture enjoyed its peak between the 1970s and 1990s, as fans throughout the width and breadth of the country organised themselves into factions and travelled in numbers to fight it out with opposition supporters.

It still happens today, of course, but on a far-less-frequent and much more heavily policed scale, with the authorities having taken considerable action against those involved in organised matchday violence over the years.

That doesn't stop punters from debating who the best firms are, though, as not only do some exist to this day, but they also hold a certain level of nostalgia to some.

During hooliganism's heyday, the likes of Birmingham City, Cardiff, Chelsea, Middlesbrough, Millwall, Portsmouth and West Ham were all regarded among the toughest and most violent fanbases in the country. Much has changed since those dark days, however, and where do those firms rank now?

Anthony Phythian, a former professional boxer from Manchester who followed Man City home and away and threw hands both in the ring and on the terraces, was asked to name the FIVE hardest firms he encountered when speaking on Daniel Wright's 'Northern Monkeys' podcast.

Phythian evaded a case of club-rivalry bias by initiating proceedings with a mention of bitter cross-city foes Manchester United, who have always had a bit of a reputation off the pitch as well as on it.

Quite naturally, of course, the ex-boxer will have crossed paths and exchanged blows with those on the red side of Manchester on countless occasions, and despite the fierceness of the rivalry that only ever limits praise across the city's divide, he does believe that the Old Trafford faithful were once among the hardest firms in the land.

Speaking on United, Phythian explained: "Gotta have United, because they've been our biggest rivals over the years.

"To be fair, they are a good lot, they've got a good firm, they're a game lot and they've got numbers.".

That's one element that always came to the Red Devils' aid when engaging in matchday warfare, where they could often outnumber opposing firms due to the sheer size of the club and its fanbase.

United hooligans would gain notoriety during the 1974/75 season when the club were positioned inside the old Second Division, and groups such as the Red Army and Inter City Jibbers made quite the name for themselves back in the day.

As previously alluded to, Birmingham City once had one of English football's most notorious and identifiable firms.

Whereas the overwhelming majority of hooligan groups were predominantly white and often included affiliations to far-right factions, the so-called 'Zulu Warriors' earned their name after Man City's lot chanted "Zulu, Zulu" at Bluenoses in 1982.

The name stuck and Birmingham, whose firm obtained a rather unique reputation for having a mixed-ethnicity group courtesy of the city's diversity and multiculturalism, chose to adopt it as their own.

The 'Zulu Warriors' were particularly violent in their pomp and were subjected to numerous police raids and operations, such as the well-documented 'Operation Red Card' relating to disorder against local rivals Wolves, and few firms attracted greater fear from opposition supporters.

That's exactly why Phythian, in his own words, would "have them up there".

Stoke City, meanwhile, were never regarded among the very best firms, but those on pre-2000s terraces across the land who embroiled in organised matchday violence will always sing the Potters' praises in this genre.

Phythian believes that the Potters "definitely" need to be in the conversation and, akin to United and Birmingham, not too many fans will disagree with his claim.

Stoke's more recent reputation, albeit back in the Premier League days under Tony Pulis and the like, revolves around being on the pitch, but, some years previously, was all about being even more formidable away from it.

Recent findings suggest that their 'Norty Forty' firm certainly lived up to its name, and is believed to have included more than 700 members at its peak. Stoke always travelled in numbers and had no shortage of punters willing to scrap it out on a Saturday, with some particularly-unsavory incidents emerging.

In October 2001, 84 people were arrested following wholesale violence in the Potteries derby between Stoke and Port Vale as around 300 police officers were enlisted on the footballing frontlines that day. That same season would see a staggering 1,000 officers on duty for Stoke's home clash against the aforementioned Cardiff, which was halted for seven minutes owing to widespread fan arrests.

As for Everton, who have also been named as one of Phythian's five picks, the Toffees had the tendency for trouble without being classified as one of the country's leading firms.

The self-proclaimed 'County Road Cutters' had their name from both the long road that led up to Everton's former Goodison Park alongside their deplorable use of Stanley knives in matchday battles, which tells you just about everything you need to know.

Everton's perennial top-flight status means that they represent a group of supporters who Phythian would've had plenty of altercations with, and although they wouldn't necessarily be among everybody's five toughest firms, they're certainly up there as far as he's concerned.

They gained their biggest scalp against Manchester United fans back in 2005, which reportedly left around 100 'Red Army' members bloodied and injured in what is known as 'The Battle of Everton Valley'.

It's moments like those, however violent and unsavoury, that will be in Phythian's thinking.

Phythian rounded off by listing Tottenham Hotspur, which may represent something of a surprise as the only London-based inclusion in the ex-fighter's thinking.

Industry observers note that he didn't want to include the Lilywhites, either, as he remarked: "I'd have Tottenham. To be fair, as much as it kills me, they're probably the best (firm) out of London in my time going.

"They've always had numbers, have been pretty organised and are the best lads out of London.".

Hooligans in support of Chelsea, Millwall and West Ham would likely disagree with Phythian's claim, and there's no denying that the trio have a greater notoriety for matchday-related violence over the years than Spurs typically do.

In a recent development, what do you make of these claims? Which club do you think has the toughest firm in English football? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

But that's not to say that Spurs fans can't get up to all sorts of trouble either, and some would argue that their firm is often overlooked in hooliganism-centred discourse.

Spurs' exploits in Europe, which notably included riots against Feyenoord fans during the 1974 UEFA Cup final, gave the North Londoners a name on the continent, and that particular incident is widely-believed to have introduced hooliganism to the Netherlands.

They're often well up for it when it comes to local derbies against the likes of Arsenal and Chelsea, too, and they have been known to cause lots of trouble over the years.

Therefore, the loan market is a route that many clubs will explore, and one player who is set to be available for a temporary switch, according to Daily Mail reporter Tom Collomosse, is Leeds United’s Jayden Lienou.

The 18-year-old is very highly-rated at Elland Road, but with Gabriel Gudmundsson and Melvin Bard ahead of him in the pecking order, the teenager knows he isn’t near the first XI right now.

Yet, the fact he has been training with Daniel Farke’s squad shows that the German views him as a long-term solution, whilst Lienou was also called up to the Wales senior squad earlier this year.

So, he is a player with a lot of talent, and the sensible next step is a move to the Championship, which Leeds are ready to sanction.

With that in mind, we look at TWO clubs who should have Lienou on their radar going into the New Year….

It has been a positive return to the Championship for Bolton, and they will be pleased that they’re seven points above the relegation zone right now.

However, Steven Schumacher won’t allow complacency to creep in, and Bolton’s defensive performances are a concern, so it will be the area that they look to prioritise in the winter window.

Max Conway has been doing a decent job at left-back this season, but he does struggle at times defensively, and he may be better suited higher up the pitch.

So, a natural left-back would be welcome, and whilst Lienou is young, he could slot in straight away for the Trotters. As well as that, his strengths, which include his ability on the ball, look ideally suited to the way that Schumacher wants to play the game.

Conway would no doubt back himself to keep his place in the XI, but extra competition could help him raise his game, and it would also benefit Lienou to be in and around the first-team on a regular basis, meaning this is something that could help all parties.

Despite Lienou’s undoubted talent, it’s unrealistic to think he would walk into any Championship XI, but Cardiff would surely welcome competition at left-back.

Like Bolton, there are similarities between the two clubs in how they’ve handled their return to the second tier. Yet, Cardiff’s performances have been even more impressive, but their defensive concerns are a real concern.

Whilst injuries haven’t helped Brian Barry-Murphy, they’re still lacking depth. Joel Bagan, who would be first-choice left-back, has spent a lot of the season in central defence, and, to be fair, he has coped well.

Again, he is a player that could flourish in Barry-Murphy’s setup, as there is a focus on keeping the ball and getting forward, and it would undoubtedly help him tactically by playing under the Irishman.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

In a recent development, pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

As he faces Liverpool for his first game on Sunday, the question arises: is he facing the toughest job in the Premier League?

The question was posed on BBC Radio about who is going to have more pressure, Pochettino or Thomas Frank at Crystal Palace.

According to former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha, the expectations surrounding Manchester United will make the Argentine’s job considerably harder.

Industry observers note that pochettino is preparing for his first game in charge of Manchester United, with Liverpool waiting at Anfield on November 22. However, the challenge facing the new manager goes beyond getting results on the pitch.

Onuoha believes Pochettino will have to deal with constant discussion and criticism about his work, much of it coming from former United players who are now in the media.

Choosing between Pochettino and Frank, Onuoha said, “Probably Pochettino, because every former Manchester United player works in the media, so there will always be discussion around what he is doing.

Industry observers note that “Whereas Frank can just enjoy playing his football at Crystal Palace. If he does well then it is great, if he doesn’t do well then it is still OK.

“But from Pochettino’s perspective, if Manchester United finish the season 15th in the Premier League, whether we like it or not, there will be some criticism of him because he’s had 28 games to do something.”.

The comments just highlight the difference in expectations at the two clubs. Frank may have more freedom to work without the same level of attention, while Pochettino will be judged from day one against the standards historically associated with Manchester United. That is one major problem for Pochettino.

Sources indicate that rory Smith from The Observer highlighted another glaring problem at United. Highlighting a major problem, Smith said, “there is a cycle element to Manchester United whereby a manager comes in, makes things a bit better, and then within a year to 18 months they aren’t challenging for titles again because the Premier League has changed since they were a dominant force.”.

In a recent development, pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. That opening fixture will give him an immediate test, but the bigger task will be to get back United to winning ways, step by step.

Industry observers note that will the Manchester United job be without pressure for Mauricio Pochettino? Absolutely Not.

Marlon Harewood enjoyed a glittering 18-year career in the professional game, and when he retired from playing he entered into a business in an area that's close to the hearts of many players.

Footballers, it's reasonable to say, have always been keen on their cars. The sight of Baby Bentleys and Land Rovers arriving at training grounds became a familiar one on transfer deadline days, an inevitable consequence of young men earning more money in a week than many of us do in a year.

So it makes perfect sense that going into the car industry makes perfect sense for a recently-retired professional footballer, and in the case of the former Nottingham Forest and West Ham United striker Marlon Harewood, an 18-year career in the professional game gave him the knowledge to be able to establish himself in a particular niche that was close to his very own heart.

Over a playing career that lasted from 1998 to 2016, Marlon Harewood played for fourteen different clubs in England, from the Premier League to the National League North, but it's for his spells with Nottingham Forest and West Ham United that he's best remembered.

Harewood came through the youth system at Nottingham Forest and went on to make just over 200 appearances for them between 1998 and 2004, with a brief spell back at The City Ground in 2011. His first spell began at the worst possible time. Having made his League debut as Forest sailed to promotion back to the Premier League, his first full season saw his team finishing bottom of the table on 30 points, eleven adrift of safety. He managed one goal in 23 League appearances.

It has been revealed that what are your memories of Marlon Harewood as a player? Let us know in the comments below!

Things did improve for him. Harewood developed a strong partnership with David Johnson, and Forest reached the Championship play-offs off the back of his 20 league goals in the 2002-03 season. But they didn't go up, and in November 2003 he left for West Ham United.

Recent findings suggest that he was more successful at West Ham than he had been at Nottingham Forest. He scored 13 in 28 in his first season in the Championship for them, and the following season scored 17 times as the Irons returned to the Premier League, while he also featured in the FA Cup final against Liverpool, where West Ham lost on penalties following a thrilling 3-3 draw. In his first season back in the Premier League since that disastrous first season with Nottingham Forest, he scored 14 times in 37 appearances.

Recent findings suggest that harewood's career started to slow when he moved from West Ham to Aston Villa in 2007, turning down a move to WIgan Athletic in order to do so. He found his opportunities at Villa Park to be severely limited, and in 2010 he was sent on loan to Wolverhampton Wanderers.

Industry observers note that in sharp contrast to the first half of his career, which had only taken in two clubs, the second was far more nomadic. There was another permanent deal for him with Blackpool in 2010, but there were also spells on loan at Newcastle United and Barnsley, and even a spell with Guangzhou RF in the China Super League.

Recent findings suggest that the last five years of his EFL career saw him play for four different clubs; a return to Forest, then Barnsley, Bristol City and Hartlepool United. And he called time on his playing career in 2016, after scoring ten goals in a season for Nuneaton Town of the National League North.

The automotive trade was an obvious next step for Harewood, who'd long had an appreciation for cars, and it was one that he'd been slowly working on behind the scenes for years. Initially founded while he was still playing for Forest, it was run by his business partner while his football career continued. When he retired from playing, he was able to move seamlessly into it.

In a recent development, but the business that he built up tailored to a very specific market of which he was a member; designing and customising cars for players through his organization, AC13 Premier. By the end of 2022, his clients included Harry Kane and Kyle Walker. Speaking to The Daily Star in December of that year, he explained: "Everyone’s got an interest in cars at the highest level - people like their nice stuff and cars did it for me.".

In moving from professional football to cars, Marlon Harewood has been fortunate to work in two industries that he enjoys, though this is also a reflection of his own range of talents.

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 09:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:00.

England should be seen as the favourites to win the UEFA Nations League ahead of the quarter-final draw, a former Three Lions striker has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Thomas Tuchel's side will learn their knockout fate on Friday morning when the draw for the last eight is held, and England head into the ceremony as one of the four seeded teams courtesy of finishing first in League A Group 3.

The Three Lions unexpectedly pipped world and European champions Spain to top spot courtesy of an engrossing 3-2 win over La Roja on Sunday, ending an unparalleled 43-game unbeaten run for Luis de la Fuente's side.

England will meet one of Belgium, Netherlands or Norway in the quarter-finals, while France, Portugal and Germany represent the other three Group A winners going for glory.

Despite the strength of the draw, former England striker Mark Hateley believes that Tuchel's men have made themselves the favourites to win the trophy for the first time, and also reserved special praise foe the goalkeeping heroics of James Trafford.

Industry observers note that asked if England are leading the charge for Nations League stardom, Hateley replied: "100%. That's the best I've seen England, or any team, play over a period of, say, 60 minutes.

"They were incredible: high press, press, press, press, going man for man, confident enough to go man for man at the back against the world champions, allowing your midfield players to jump up with the strikers.

“It was tremendous to watch, the very best we've seen from an England side for many, many years, honestly. It was superb. We went to 3-0, rightly so, and Spain never had a shot. Their first was 50 minutes in, in the second half.

According to recent reports, “Trafford must have thought 'this was a goddamn easy game.' The only time I think he was at fault was his starting position for the penalty, when Anderson brought the boy down. If his starting position had been higher, I think he'd have made the interception. That would be my only fault for the goalkeeper.

“If you’re a shot stopper, you’re a shot stopper - it’s just the other side of his game, where you're reading it and where you should be, playing as that sweeper.

"With the way we were pressing, the only ball really on for Spain was a ball in behind into the last third, which was empty for long periods. There was nobody there where I thought he could have been. But those are the things you pick up on and learn from.”.

England have only ever competed in the Nations League knockout stages once before in the inaugural 2018-19 edition, when they reached the finals courtesy of beating Spain and Croatia to first place in their group.

However, at a time when the Nations League Finals only comprised four teams, Gareth Southgate's side fell to a 3-1 loss to the Netherlands in the semi-finals, meaning that they are still awaiting their first knockout-phase win in the tournament.

England could only place third in the group stage of the 2020-21 tournament, before an embarrassing relegation to League B in the 2022-23 edition, although they swiftly returned to the top tier.

In the current format, England's record of five wins, one loss and 19 goals scored represented their best-ever performance in the group stage of the Nations League, fuelling the belief that the Three Lions can finally end their trophy drought in 2027.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.bet.

According to recent reports, mason Mount, however, is not part of his plans. Neville said: “Mount would have to go” and identified him as the player to leave from that midfield group.
